ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Under UIAF rules and Decreto 1074 de 2015, the S.A.S. must screen every shareholder, UBO, director and legal representative against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the UIAF Colombian PEP list, the Procuraduría/Contraloría ineligibility lists, and the Colombian National Police terrorist watchlist. Screening is mandatory at incorporation, before any capital increase or share transfer, and at least monthly thereafter. Results must be retained for five years and made available to the Superintendencia de Sociedades and UIAF on request.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) and the online homonymy-certificate system of the competent Cámara de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name (razón social or denominación) must be expressed in Spanish using the Latin alphabet. Foreign descriptive terms may be used only with a Spanish translation or clear phonetic transliteration. Chinese logograms are not accepted in the registered name; accents and punctuation must follow Spanish orthographic rules and the name must not be unduly similar to existing registered commercial names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within ten business days of a name-rejection notice, the incorporator may file a recurso de reposición before the competent Cámara de Comercio and, subsidiarily, a recurso de apelación before the Superintendencia de Sociedades. The appeal must include the RUES rejection code, the proposed corrected name, and evidence of the homonymy search. A name reservation may generally be renewed for one additional 30-day period by submitting a renewal application before expiry of the original reservation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is acceptable only as the formal statutory domicile for receiving service of process and administrative notices. The Malatang restaurant must nonetheless maintain a physical commercial premises satisfying municipal zoning, public health, fire-safety and employment-workplace requirements. A virtual office alone is therefore not permissible as the principal place of business for a food-service operation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-high. Estimated 55% probability of an unannounced municipal health inspection within the first 12 months of operation due to food handling; 30% probability of an unannounced labor or social-security inspection; and approximately 10% probability of a corporate-registry verification of the registered domicile. The entity should retain active compliance insurance and maintain premises open and accessible during normal business hours.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), arts. 1-46; Código de Comercio (Decreto 410 de 1971), arts. 19, 98-119; Decreto Único Reglamentario 1074 de 2015, arts. 2.2.2.1.1 et seq.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social; in Bogotá D.C., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá; registries consolidated through RUES (Registro Único Empresarial); Superintendencia de Sociedades supervises S.A.S.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private constitutional instrument registered in the Mercantile Registry; public deed is required if real property is contributed)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum legal capital for S.A.S.; capital and payment deadlines are freely established in the bylaws, but outstanding contributions must be paid within one year; no statutory escrow account mandatory; shares must be fully subscribed and issued following Law 1258 of 2008.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: First Board Resolution. 1. Share Subscriptions: The board accepts the full subscription of [X] ordinary shares at [COP Y] per share; contributions and payment terms are recorded in the share ledger. 2. Registered Office: The registered office is fixed at [address], and the legal representative is authorized to execute the lease and municipal permits. 3. Appointments: [Shareholder A] is elected Legal Representative; [Shareholder B] is elected Compliance/Financial Officer. 4. Implementation: The Legal Representative is authorized to file statutory forms, obtain tax and registry certificates, open bank accounts, and hire personnel. 5. Ratification: All above resolutions are declared valid and irrevocable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name availability search and corporate bylaws draft
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá / RUES online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access RUES and submit up to three proposed names for a homonymy certificate; prepare the S.A.S. bylaws including corporate purpose for fast-casual self-serve broth-bowl restaurant operation and brand licensing, duration, capital, management, and audit clauses. Notarization is optional unless real property is contributed.
required_dossiers: Name pre-validation request or homonymy certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to homonymy, immediately file an alternative name; correct observations in RUES and resubmit for re-certification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (if real assets) or private signatures; subsequently Cámara de Comercio
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All shareholders execute the incorporation instrument, explicitly subscribe shares and indicate their paid-up portion, payment date, and form of payment. If real property is contributed, the instrument must be converted into a public deed before a Notary.
required_dossiers: Share subscription and payment schedule annex
Notarial certificate if public deed is required
Payment evidence for subscribed capital if paid at signing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the chamber or notary finds signature defects, re-execute the relevant pages and obtain apostille or notarization before refiling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mercantile registry registration and corporate existence certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social / RUES
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation instrument in the Mercantile Registry within 30 days of execution; pay registration tariff; obtain certificate of incorporation (Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal), register legal books and legal representative data.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues an inadmissibility order, comply with the corrections or contest within the legal term; re-register after curing defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax identification and RUT registration at DIAN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales) via RUES or DIAN portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of registration, complete the RUT update to obtain NIT, constitute the S.A.S. as an income taxpayer, and select the applicable tax regime; request the electronic invoicing authorization if the company will operate before full licensing.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DIAN rejects or suspends the RUT, use the correction procedure through RUES; file a written clarification to DIAN and update the responsible fiscal information.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Employer registration and social security affiliation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: PILA (Planilla Integrada de Liquidación de Aportes); Caja de Compensación Familiar; ARL insurer selected
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the S.A.S. as employer before EPS, ARL, pension fund and family compensation fund; enroll workers under Colombia Labor Code; create the PILA payroll settlement account; set occupational risk class for restaurant/cooking activities.
required_dossiers: Employee labor contracts and personal data
ARL affiliation selection and workplace risk assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If PILA payments are rejected due to invalid affiliation, correct employer data in the payroll portal, re-submit adjusted PILA, and obtain written approval from the ARL.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Secretaría Distrital de Salud (District Health Secretariat); INVIMA (Instituto Nacional de Vigilancia de Medicamentos y Alimentos) for packaged food products and imported condiment products
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Concepto Sanitario Favorable / Sanitary operating permit for restaurants and retail food service; municipal land-use and commercial operating license (Licencia de Funcionamiento de Comercio) and food handling certification

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) with local support from Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 4 / Low-Impact Registration category; food-service establishment normally requires simplified environmental declaration and no full EIA report unless daily wastewater volume or grease emissions exceed Resolution 1208 of 2000 thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: comply with Resolution 0631 of 2015 discharge limits; grease traps installed and cleaned under municipal grease-management rules. Air/VOC: Resolution 2254 of 2017 for air quality; indoor cooking ventilation standards. Solid waste: separate ordinary/food waste per Decree 2981 of 2013; used cooking oil managed under Resolution 4741 of 2005 hazardous-waste rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos; structural load inspection and building usability certificate; evacuation plan; occupational health and safety program registration with the ARL; local police or administrative clearance for public operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN); official portal: https://www.dian.gov.co and Sede Electrónica (MUISCA platform).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a Colombian S.A.S. must: (1) execute and notarize the bylaws, then register the company with the Cámara de Comercio to obtain the commercial registration and the electronic 'firma electrónica' certificate; (2) appoint a legal representative domiciled in Colombia with apostilled and protocolized power of attorney; (3) file the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) pre-registration through the MUISCA portal, attaching the apostilled certificate of incorporation, the power of attorney, and any foreign investment registration with the Banco de la República; (4) obtain the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) from DIAN and select the applicable tax responsibilities on the RUT, including 'Responsable de IVA' status for taxable sales and services; (5) complete the electronic invoicing habilitación process and issue invoices exclusively in the DIAN-approved electronic system before the first transaction.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or pass-through election exists for a Colombian S.A.S.; the entity is always taxed at entity level under Article 4 of Law 1258/2008. Available statutory elections include: (i) the elective Régimen Simple de Tributación (SIMPLE) for eligible small taxpayers under Articles 905-915 ET, generally unsuitable for a royalty-licensing fast-casual franchise model; (ii) optional alignment of accounting closing and CIT filing to the calendar year; (iii) the election to treat qualifying offshore franchise fees and support services as zero-rated 'servicios exportados' under the special VAT export rules; and (iv) transfer-pricing simplification elections consistent with Colombian transfer-pricing documentation rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto sobre las Ventas - IVA (Colombian Value Added Tax / VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de minimis turnover threshold applies to VAT registration in Colombia; the statutory trigger is the habitual performance of taxable transactions (sale of goods or provision of services) within the national territory, irrespective of revenue volume. A foreign entity with a fixed place of business or performing taxable activities in Colombia must register in the RUT as 'Responsable de IVA' before the first taxable transaction. Non-resident digital service suppliers have a separate registration obligation under Decree 358/2020.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time electronic invoicing ('factura electrónica de venta') applies to all VAT-responsible businesses. Invoices must be generated in DIAN-approved XML format containing CUF and CUDE codes, transmitted immediately for online validation clearance to the DIAN through authorized software providers' SOAP/REST APIs, and display a scannable QR code. The DIAN must issue the acceptance ('acuse de recibo') or rejection ('tachamiento') event before the invoice acquires fiscal validity; deadlines for daily transmission are prescribed by DIAN. Purchases from non-obligated suppliers require the electronic 'documento soporte en adquisiciones a no obligados' filed and stored in the RADIAN archive.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Physical exports of goods are excluded from IVA at the 0% rate and carry the right to obtain a refund of input VAT. Intangible services, including franchise royalties and software-support services, qualify as zero-rated 'servicios exportados' when cumulatively: (i) the service is rendered to a foreign recipient not established in Colombia; (ii) the benefit is realized and consumed outside Colombia; (iii) the service is not physically performed in connection with movable or immovable property located in Colombia; and (iv) the exporter maintains contractual, performance, transfer-pricing and foreign-exchange repatriation evidence. For the Malatang self-serve fast-casual franchise, local franchise royalties on Colombian store sales remain taxable at 19%, while qualifying offshore licensing and management-support fees may be zero-rated if the statutory export-service criteria are met.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Declaración de Exportación (DEX) validated by DIAN customs for goods, or the documented service-export dossier for intangible services
Bill of Lading (maritime) or Airway Bill (air) evidencing the physical exit of goods, or the service delivery/consumption certificates for export services
Inward Remittance Certificate / certificado de canalización de divisas issued by a Colombian intermediary financial institution evidencing repatriation through the foreign-exchange market
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN audits export zero-rating claims strictly. The taxpayer inaccuracy penalty under Article 648 ET is 100% of the understated VAT, escalating to 200% for recurring or documentary-fraud patterns; improper refunds face the Article 674 ET penalty of 20% plus default interest. Retrospective clawbacks extend through the standard 4-year statute of limitations for filed returns, expanded to 6 or 8 years where a return was not filed or foreign assets/income were omitted. Criminal prosecution under Article 402(2) of the Colombian Criminal Code may apply for aggravated tax evasion involving forged export evidence. The taxpayer carries the burden of proving effective exportation, foreign consumption and FX repatriation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República (Central Bank of Colombia) together with the Comité de Cambios (Foreign Exchange Committee) and the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit. Operational enforcement is delegated to the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC) and the Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso (COP, ISO 4217 code COP) is freely convertible for current-account transactions, including royalties, service fees, dividends, and profit remittances, provided the transactions are channeled through an authorized financial intermediary registered with Banco de la República. Capital-account convertibility is subject to a prior declaration of foreign direct investment (FDI) through the 'Declaración de Cambio por Inversiones Internacionales' with the applicable statistical category codes. For an SAS engaged in a fast-casual Chinese malatang self-serve franchise, inbound equity or shareholder loan injections may be treated as FDI capital inflows, requiring registration with the Central Bank's 'Registro de Inversiones Internacionales' (Foreign Investment Register) within the statutory timeframe. Profit remittance and dividend repatriation to non-resident shareholders are generally unrestricted once taxes are paid and compliance formalities are met; however, remittance must be executed via an authorized FX intermediary and reported using the appropriate 'Declaración de Cambio' form. Repatriation obstacles may appear if the company fails to submit annual or semi-annual 'CERO' forms (offshore foreign investment updates) or if the original FDI registration was incomplete.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Colombia's foreign exchange regime (Régimen Cambiario), export proceeds from goods and services must be 'canalized' (surrendered or collected) through authorized FX intermediaries. For services exports, including franchise fees, royalties, and licensing income received by a Colombian entity from outside, the proceeds must be received in Colombia and reported via the 'Declaración de Cambio' within the general settlement deadline of six (6) months from the date of issue of the export invoice or the service billing, unless a specific extension is granted by Banco de la República. For goods exports (if any ancillary merchandise supplied to the franchise), the exporter must surrender 100% of the export value within the statutory term, normally six months, but DIAN/Banco de la República may apply shorter periods for perishable or certain identified operations. Mandatory conversion of COP from export proceeds into foreign currency is not required; the obligation is to channel funds through the controlled FX market and declare them, not to monetize into COP automatically. Failure to timely canalize triggers fines calculated by Banco de la República and potential adverse tax treatment under Colombian transfer pricing rules.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Cuenta de Ahorros / Cuenta Corriente) in COP and USD
Capital Escrow Account (Cuenta de Interés y Custodia) and Operational Account
Operational Account with POS settlement and royalty wire receipt
Operational Account (only if treasury requirements align with Scotiabank's international network)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for a newly formed Colombian SAS. Offshore digital electronic money institutions (EMIs) and virtual account providers are not recognized as authorized FX intermediaries under Colombian law and cannot settle 'Declaración de Cambio' obligations. To receive inbound FDI or pay cross-border trade disbursements in a compliant manner, funds must flow through a supervised financial institution (credit establishment or exchange house) registered before Banco de la República. Local Fintechs licensed as Sociedades Especializadas en Depósitos y Pagos Electrónicos (SEDPE) may provide operational payment accounts and POS aggregation, but they cannot independently satisfy statutory FX reporting for shareholder loans or royalty remittances. Therefore, the treasury architecture must combine a regulated Tier-1 bank for all FX and cross-border flows with a local licensed Fintech only for domestic low-value settlement (e.g., POS payments and small supplier payments).
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Colombian anti-money laundering rules generally require the legal representative(s) and, in most cases, all direct shareholders holding 5% or more or those exercising effective control to undergo an in-person KYC interview at the bank branch or, under certain digital onboarding regimes for 'low-risk' clients, a remotely verified video interview with a dynamic notarial acknowledgment. For a foreign-owned SAS controlled by non-resident Chinese shareholders, physical presence in Colombia is normally required for the first onboarding: the legal representative (even if the representative is a non-resident) must attend in person with the original notarized and apostilled incorporation documents, company bylaws, tax identification certificate (NIT), and proof of actual corporate address. Remote opening is possible for local directors who already have a Colombian national ID and are force-listed with a local registrar, provided the bank's risk model permits 'Banca Virtual' for non-complex enterprises; nevertheless, for the capital escrow account, the SFC's 'Customers' Due Diligence' standards compel a minimum of one in-person executive session. To mitigate travel burdens, the shareholders may appoint a local legal representative with a Colombian residence and an especial power that explicitly grants banking opening authority, while the foreign shareholder(s) submit apostilled powers and identity documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident Chinese shareholders with opaque holding structure or without clear economic substance in China
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide group organizational chart, audited financial statements of ultimate individual shareholders (redacted), Chinese business license, passport copies, tax residency certificates, and a corporate narrative outlining the commercial rationale for establishing the Colombian SAS as the Latin American franchise master. Also include affidavit of ultimate beneficial ownership signed by each direct/indirect shareholder holding >5%.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection expected from China to fund the 'Capital Escrow Account' without a local salary or payroll history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a board resolution approving the FDI, bank cover letter with the exact purpose code (e.g., '191: Capital por Inversión Directa'), financing source documents (bank account statement of shareholder, transaction title, source-of-wealth letter), and a signed undertaking to submit the 'Declaración de Cambio por Inversiones Internacionales' within thirty (30) days of the wire. Add a pre-issued local employee roster to demonstrate genuine operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Royalty and licensing fee outflows to Chinese parent or related suppliers generating high cross-border volume
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide executed license/trademark agreement, valuation report (transfer pricing study), descriptions of support functions performed by the Chinese counterparty, expatriate employment agreements, and a written commitment to issue monthly 'Declaraciones de Cambio' with consistent concept codes. For services over USD 50,000 equivalent, attach an invoice with breakdown of hours or deliverables.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts of directors for storage or distribution of franchise cash flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Implement a board-approved treasury policy prohibiting the use of personal accounts for corporate receipts, include a sworn statement of account segregation, and present the opening of dedicated corporate accounts at two regulated banks. Submit a notarized 'Know Your Business' questionnaire covering business activities, expected transaction volumes, and gateway channels.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sectoral licensing (food franchise/restaurant) not visible in corporate documents causing suspicion of illegal activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present the municipal health and food safety permits (Registro Sanitario), the trademark registration with Supersociedades/DIAN, the signed franchise master agreement, and the lease of the physical premises. For the specific malatang fast-casual self-serve concept, provide a detailed food import list, alcohol nil policy, and hygiene audit evidence.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound invested capital must be structured as direct foreign investment (inversión extranjera directa) received via SWIFT MT103 in COP or USD from the Chinese parent. The remitter must use a clear wire purpose: 'Shareholder Loan to Colombian Subsidiary' or 'Equity Contribution for Working Capital' as appropriate. On receipt, the local bank will require the submission of the 'Declaración de Cambio' using concept code '191' for equity capital, '192' for loan in foreign currency, or '193' for loan in legal tender from abroad, whichever corresponds. The bank credits the funds into a central operational account; at the same time the company must register the investment in Banco de la República's Investment Register within 30 calendar days of receipt. To avoid over-yielding against the 'capital escrow' classification, the account should clearly flag that the net proceeds are earmarked for approved expenditure only, and a redemption request (for liquidation) will require a 'Certificado de Devolución de Capital' from the registrant. For contracts, the parent should execute a zero-interest or market-rate shareholder loan agreement, evidencing term, principal amount, and repayment mechanics; all documentation must be apostilled in China and available in Spanish upon request.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for equipment, spices, condiments, and commercial capital goods purchased from China or other suppliers will be executed through (1) standard SWIFT MT103 payments for advance payment terms, open account, or post-shipment settlement; (2) irrevocable and confirmed Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C at sight or usance) for significant production runs, where the Colombian SAS opens an import LC at Bancolombia or Banco de Bogotá and China counterparties negotiate against documents; and (3) documentary collections (D/P, D/A) for medium-risk trade. For intercompany royalties, disbursements are made via SWIFT MT103 using the payment description 'Royalties under License Agreement' and the relevant 'Declaración de Cambio' concept code for patent/trademark royalties (category 'Residenciados en el exterior – Regalías'). Cross-border clearing rails must always include a 'Tramitación de Operación' through the local bank's foreign trade desk, and each transaction must be paired with the corresponding DIAN import declaration (Declaración de Importación) or an exemption certificate when only ingressing software (as a service). Domestic outbound payments for rent, wages, utility, and POS settlements flow over the local ACH (CENIT), check, or bank debit routes, using the same COP account as the operational treasury account. The treasury policy should centralize all 'draft' and 'incoming wire' accounts in one bank to minimize FX conversion costs.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Delivery FX Forwards (USD/COP) on professional terms with a local supervised bank, recorded as hedging instruments under the corporate's derivative policy, permissible for up to 12 months; require an underlying commercial/financial exposure in USD, COP, CNY, or other foreign currency.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) with licensed local banks against COP, permitted only where the counterparty is subject to Colombian financial regulation and the contract is treated as a hedging derivative; settlement is in COP against COP/USD reference rate published by Banco de la República.

Cross-currency Swaps (XCCY) between COP and USD for syndicated loans or large shareholder loans, subject to SFC approval and compliance with the risk management framework; generally only for sophisticated corporations with an existing derivative master agreement (ISDA).

Plain Vanilla Currency Options (FX Options) USD/COP permitted as over-the-counter contracts with a local financial institution for hedging liquidity risk, with the condition that the counterparty is a supervised entity and positions are reported under Colombian favorability rules.

Currency Swaps with financial institutions to convert a shareholder loan denominated in CNY or USD into COP liabilities, permissibly used only when the underlying exposure is documented and the transaction does not create an unregistered lien against assets requiring notarization.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registry Renewal (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the registered domicile, e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal after 31 March triggers a late-filing surcharge computed on the current Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio tariff; two consecutive years without renewal entitle the Chamber of Commerce to close the mercantile registration, resulting in administrative strike-off and loss of the S.A.S.'s legal capacity to operate, invoice, or open bank accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary Shareholders' Meeting and Approval of Financial Statements (Asamblea General Ordinaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate corporate books; minutes of the meeting kept in the Minute Book and filed with the Chamber of Commerce where required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 March annually within the first quarter of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the meeting and approve the annual financial statements by 31 March restricts lawful profit distribution and may trigger Chamber of Commerce warnings; persistent non-compliance for two consecutive fiscal years contributes to administrative strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements as of 31 December (Estados Financieros de Cierre)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the registered domicile, attached to the commercial registry renewal packet
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March, signed by the legal representative and, when applicable, by the public accountant or Revisor Fiscal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Financial statements not filed by the renewal deadline leave the registration incomplete; the S.A.S. cannot lawfully distribute profits, and the Chamber may downgrade the renewal status and proceed to registry closure after two years of omitted filings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner Declaration (Declaración Anual de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN - Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales, electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 July per DIAN Resolution No. 000164 of 2021, subject to the NIT-digit peak calendar fixed by DIAN
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-submission or materially inaccurate submission is penalized under Article 651 of the Colombian Tax Statute with fines of up to 38,000 UVT (approximately USD 458,000 in 2024); repeated irregularity also elevates UIAF anti-money-laundering scrutiny and banking due-diligence risk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta, Form 210)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN - Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales, electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in April; the exact due date is assigned by the last two digits of the NIT in the applicable DIAN resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of the assessed tax for each month or partial month of delay, capped at 100% of the tax due; unpaid balances additionally accrue monthly default interest, and the S.A.S. temporarily loses access to certain tax benefits until the return is filed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Exogenous Information Return (Información Exógena, Formats 2276-2279)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN - Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales, electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in March and April according to the NIT-digit calendar published by DIAN
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit, late submission, or material errors are penalized under Article 651 of the Tax Statute with fines up to 38,000 UVT; continued non-compliance may also result in suspension of electronic invoicing authorizations and inclusion in DIAN's high-risk registries.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Municipal Industry and Commerce Tax (ICA) Declaration and Payment, applicable where the S.A.S. derives royalty or franchise-service income in a Colombian municipality
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipal fiscal authority / Secretaría de Hacienda of the domicile municipality
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between February and April, following the municipal filing calendar; most municipalities require submission by late April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfiled or late-filed ICA triggers a late-filing penalty of 5% of the tax per month of delay, subject to a 100% cap, plus default interest; continued non-payment leads to municipal collection proceedings and may affect the validity of the franchise's operating licenses.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A S.A.S. must appoint a Revisor Fiscal (statutory auditor) when, as of 31 December of the immediately preceding year: (i) gross total assets exceed 5,000 monthly minimum legal wages (SMMLV), approximately COP 6.5 billion or USD 1.6 million for fiscal year 2024; or (ii) annual gross revenues exceed 3,000 SMMLV, approximately COP 3.9 billion or USD 1.0 million in 2024, per Law 1258/2008, Código de Comercio Article 203, and Law 43/1990 Article 13. Below these thresholds the audit is optional unless required by the company's by-laws or by the shareholders in consideration of franchising volumes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian statutory accounting standards issued under Law 1314/2009: full IFRS for Grupo 1 large entities, and NIIF para PYMES (IFRS for SMEs) for the typical S.A.S. master franchisor classified as Grupo 2. Financial statements must be prepared in Colombian pesos and filed in Spanish, with comparative prior-year figures.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Before 31 July of each year, the S.A.S. must file with DIAN a sworn annual declaration of all ultimate beneficial owners — natural persons holding or controlling, directly or indirectly, 20% or more of shares, voting rights, economic benefits, or final control — as of 31 December of the preceding tax year. Every share transfer during the year must be recorded in the nominal shareholders' register and updated in the Chamber of Commerce registration; the annual DIAN UBO declaration must thereafter reflect the year-end ownership chain. Non-resident shareholders are permitted under Colombian law, but the local filing agent must evidence the complete chain of ownership for foreign investors and update the records upon any disposal or acquisition of quotas or shares.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Accionistas)
Register of Directors (Libro de Actas de la Junta Directiva)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas de la Asamblea)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700-2,200 per year; typical annual fee for a registered agent and legal compliance representative in Bogotá, Medellín, or Cali, including Chamber of Commerce attendance, corporate document custody, and filing assistance
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000-10,000 per year for a certified public accountant serving as Revisor Fiscal, depending on total assets, number of shareholders, and franchise royalty volume; for non-audited S.A.S. entities, a compilation or review by a local accountant typically ranges from USD 1,200-2,500

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No sector-specific statutory tax holiday for restaurant/franchise operations; general Colombian Tax Code deductions may apply, including the 50% deduction for investments in new real productive fixed assets and the payroll tax credit for additional new employment. Incentives are not industry-specific and require timely annual election.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 110 (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios) filed through the DIAN electronic portal (MUISCA) at www.dian.gov.co
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within the month of April following the fiscal year-end; DIAN assigns a specific date based on the last two digits of the taxpayer's NIT (tax identification number), generally between April 9 and April 19.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All taxable gross income from the franchise license, self-serve malatang restaurant operations, and any other Colombian-source business income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Colombian SAS files this return as a resident entity. Non-resident shareholders with no permanent establishment in Colombia are not required to file Form 110 and should not report this income on any local form.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs of operating the self-serve franchise master licensing, including depreciation, maintenance, overhead, and statutory financial expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions claimed must be supported by invoices issued in Colombia or proper foreign vendor documentation; non-resident-related expenses require withholding tax compliance and may be capped under thin capitalization rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Result after subtracting costs and deductions from gross income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is an internal calculation; no separate non-resident entry is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after applying net operating loss carryforwards (up to 12 years) and special deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders should not have branch-office income included here unless they are engaged in Colombia through a permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax due, calculated at 35% on net taxable income, less any prepayments or withholding credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign shareholders receiving a dividend will be subjected to dividend withholding at 10% at the distribution source, not on this Form 110.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing incurs a penalty of 5% of the amount of tax due for each month or fraction of delay, capped at 100% of the tax. If no tax is due, a fixed monthly penalty of approximately COP 6,000 (inflation-adjusted) applies. Late payment of the assessed tax additionally accrues daily statutory interest on arrears.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding on gross dividends paid to non-resident beneficial owners; entity-level CIT (35%) is levied on distributable profits first.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced dividend rate under a double tax agreement, the foreign beneficial owner must obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the tax authority of its country of residence and submit a standard DTA relief request to the Colombian payer before distribution. The payer submits a copy, along with an affidavit of beneficial ownership, to DIAN and applies the reduced rate if the request is conditionally accepted. Under several of Colombia's DTAs, the rate may drop to 5% for qualifying substantial shareholdings.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on royalties for trademarks, know-how, and technical assistance paid to non-residents is 15%. Statutory withholding on interest paid to non-resident lenders is also 15%, reduced to 5% for loans extended by foreign financial institutions. DTA benefits may lower these statutory rates to 10% or 5% depending on the specific treaty, the type of income, and the recipient's beneficial-ownership status.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: COP 7,766,000,000 (approximately USD 1.9 million) for fiscal year 2024; the Colombian threshold is 165,000 UVT (Unidad de Valor Tributario). A taxpayer whose total gross income or total assets exceed this threshold and who has intercompany transactions must prepare and file Local File documentation. Master File is also mandatory for multinational groups with consolidated group revenue exceeding the higher threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia applies a General Anti-Abuse Rule and the economic-substance doctrine. Franchise royalty structures that lack substantive local management, physical operations, actual employees, and a commercial purpose may be recharacterized by DIAN, and treaty benefits may be denied when the Colombian licensee or the foreign licensor lacks beneficiary ownership. The OECD/G20 minimum standards are also mirrored in Colombia's administrative rules, requiring a clear corporate purpose and real activity for any intra-group licence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally excluding cash register receipts from self-serve malatang operations or understating royalty income received from franchisees to DIAN, including failure to report all daily sales and credit-card settlement data.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine equal to 200% of the tax deficit (non-compensable with subsequent losses) plus statutory interest; criminal sanction of 6 to 9 years in prison under Article 426 of the Colombian Criminal Code for willful non-declaration of taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or approve the defective return are jointly and severally liable for the fine. In criminal proceedings, they are subject to travel bans, disqualification from managing any legal entity, and up to 9 years of imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging intra-group franchise or royalty fees to or from related parties at non-arm's-length rates, or failing to prepare and file the Local File / Master File when the applicable revenue or asset threshold is met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN may make a secondary adjustment by applying the arm's-length price and impose a penalty equal to 200% of the understated tax, or a monthly penalty equal to 5% of the value of the transactions not disclosed in the required transfer pricing return, capped at 100% of the unreported amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve intercompany pricing without a compliant benchmarking study, or who sign a false transfer-pricing certificate, are personally liable for the adjustment and corresponding fine. They also face administrative disqualification and criminal prosecution for facilitating tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Colombian S.A.S. solely as an invoicing and royalty-pass-through vehicle for an offshore principal, without local employees, an office, real business decisions, or any presence at the franchise locations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN applies the General Anti-Abuse Rule to disregard the conduit entity and reattributes the income to the true foreign recipient. The remittances are then recharacterised as dividends or royalties taxed at the regular 10% and 15% withholding rates, plus a 100% to 200% penalty on the withholding differential. All treaty relief is denied.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The directors who facilitated the sham structure are subject to corporate-veil piercing for the unpaid withholding taxes in the full amount, restrictive travel measures to secure collection, and, if laundering criminal proceeds through the entity is proven, up to 14 years in prison on money-laundering charges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Handling untraceable cash transactions at franchised self-serve kiosks without operating a suspicious-transaction monitoring program, and repeatedly splitting daily deposits below the currency transaction reporting threshold to evade UIAF oversight.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 526 of 1999 and UIAF regulations, fines of up to 100,000 legal monthly minimum wage units (about COP 116 billion for 2024) per violation per franchisee, plus a criminal sentence of 5 to 10 years for wilful concealment of illicit financial operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Each director has an independent statutory obligation to institute an AML compliance programme for the SAS and its franchise network. Failure to comply, or deliberate structuring to hide the true transaction volume, subjects the director to civil liability for the total assets moved through the system, a court-issued travel ban, and criminal extradition risk in cases involving foreign parties.
